machines: AWS EC2 us-east-2a: s1, s2 mac-m4.metal (Apple M4, 10-core GPU, 24 GB, 120 GB/s) as Dedicated Hosts ($1.23/h each, 24-hour minimum), macOS 26.7.3 (amzn-ec2-macos-26.7.3-20261120), 200 GB gp3 root volumes; router, HAProxy and load generator on r1, a c7i.xlarge (Ubuntu 24.04) in the same subnet. Scaled down from docs/plans/aws-mac-fleet-benchmark.md's six-host fleet to one identical pair, by decision (the 24-hour minimum makes every host a full day's charge however short the test). mac-m4pro.metal was the first choice and had no capacity in any of 11 zones (us-east-1a-d, us-west-2a-d, us-east-2a-c) at 20:41-20:47 UTC
ollama: 0.40.13 from the GitHub release zip, run as a LaunchDaemon by scripts/aws-mac-bootstrap.sh, with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4, OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1, OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=10, OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=4096 on both Macs (as run 5; launch args -c 16384 -np 4, ollama ps 100% GPU on both)
workload: qwen2.5:7b (Q4_K_M, 5.6 GB loaded, 100% GPU on both): qwen3-coder:30b does not fit a 24 GB M4's GPU, and a first attempt with qwen2.5:14b and 60 s cells was aborted after one cell (about 25-30 s per request, so 2-3 requests per cell; its reports are kept apart, not summarized); about 1,250 prompt and 200 completion tokens per chat request (--prompt-tokens 1250 --max-tokens 200)
telemetry: off on the router and both nodes
herd: ollama-herd 0.12.12 from PyPI on both nodes. Router: 0.12.12 from PyPI (scaling, identical_machines); 6dbf115 from 22:31 UTC (queue-concurrency fix found by this run); 87e3bf0 from the mixed_models switch (load-gate fix found by this run). Neither fix is released; both include the [Unreleased] fixes at 63a125b; 82fdf26 from 03:47 UTC (dashboard fix only, routing identical to 87e3bf0)
cache_note: Ollama's llama.cpp keeps up to 8 GiB of earlier prompts in host RAM, and the harness's prompts repeat by seed. Arms run back to back with a reused seed inherited each other's prompt cache (up to 2x more requests): scaling, scaling_fixed, identical_machines, identical_machines_fixed. From saturation on, Ollama was restarted on every Mac before every cell or run (cache empty), and those are the figures to quote

scaling.what: qwen2.5:7b on s1 alone, then s1 + s2 (s2's herd-node stopped for the one-machine cells, its Ollama left running but unknown to the router); concurrency 1, 2, 4, 8; 120 s per cell; 3 repetitions (seeds 7, 11, 13), each repetition running all one-machine cells, then all two-machine cells; herd 0.12.12 held every node to queue concurrency 1 here (see scaling_fixed)

scaling_fixed.what: as scaling, same seeds and order, with the router switched to 6dbf115 at 22:31 UTC (the Macs unchanged); /fleet/queue showed qwen2.5:7b concurrency 4 before the first cell
scaling_fixed.router: ollama-herd 6dbf115 (main, unreleased: a resident model gets every slot Ollama admits)

identical_machines.what: one model on two identical M4 Macs, 8 concurrent qwen2.5:7b, 120 s, 3 repetitions per front door (seeds 7, 11, 13), alternating Herd and HAProxy (HAProxy 2.8.30 from Ubuntu 24.04, roundrobin over both Macs' :11434, fleet state polled through the herd router with --fleet-url)

identical_machines_fixed.what: as identical_machines, with the router at 6dbf115; HAProxy re-run alternating with it so drift lands on both

saturation_np4.what: two Macs past Ollama's 4 slots each: concurrency 16 and 32, qwen2.5:7b, 120 s, 3 repetitions (seeds 7, 11, 13); Ollama restarted on both Macs before every cell. A first attempt without restarts was aborted after 2 cells (cache carry-over: 48 vs 76 requests at 4 slots); its reports are kept apart

saturation_np8.what: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL raised 4 -> 8 on both Macs (LaunchDaemon environment edited, Ollama and herd-node restarted; launch args -c 32768 -np 8, herd num_parallel 8, queue concurrency 8 checked); two Macs at concurrency 8, 16, 32 and one Mac (s2's herd-node stopped) at 8, 16; 120 s, 3 repetitions (seeds 7, 11, 13), Ollama restarted before every cell. The driver stopped once at 01:10 (a launchd restart race in the driver, not herd) and resumed for the last 3 cells

head_to_head.what: Herd vs HAProxy roundrobin on two identical M4 Macs, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4, 8 concurrent qwen2.5:7b, 120 s; Ollama restarted on both Macs before every run (prompt cache empty), each Herd/HAProxy pair on the same new seed (101, 102, 103), alternating, 3 repetitions. The clean version of identical_machines

memory_pressure.what: s1 alone (s2's herd-node stopped), 24 GB: qwen2.5:7b resident, then qwen2.5:14b loaded beside it (3.0 GB left), then a cold gemma3:12b with X-Fleet-No-Fallback; heartbeat memory sampled every 5 s through the router. Router 6dbf115: macOS pressure stayed normal throughout and herd refused gemma3:12b (All 2 nodes eliminated, 503 after the 30 s hold) although evicting either idle model fits it, the load-gate bug fixed in 87e3bf0; repeated on 87e3bf0 as pressure2_s1.json

embeddings.what: qwen2.5:7b and dinov2-vit-s14 together, 4 and 16 workers per model, 120 s, 3 repetitions each (seeds 241-243, 361-363). nomic-embed-text was requested too, but the harness at 63a125b could not see herd's native text-embedding sidecar and printed 'not loaded or on disk anywhere: nomic-embed-text': this arm has NO text embeddings. Fixed in 6a588a8 and re-run as embeddings_with_nomic

embeddings_with_nomic.what: as embeddings, with native nomic-embed-text actually included (harness 6a588a8): qwen2.5:7b + nomic-embed-text + dinov2-vit-s14, 4 and 16 workers per model, 120 s, 3 repetitions each (seeds 641-643, 761-763), Ollama restarted on both Macs first

soak.what: 4 hours, open loop 0.12 requests/s: qwen2.5:7b=6, qwen2.5:14b=1, nomic-embed-text=3, dinov2-vit-s14=1, prompt 1,250 / reply 200 tokens, timeout 600 s, seed 777, harness 1445755; /fleet/status every 10 minutes in soak_status.jsonl. Started 05:20 UTC after two false starts: the harness dropped nomic-embed-text at warmup (fixed in 1445755; a 20 s check then answered 4/4 text embeddings), and its chat-only fallback ran on a 24 GB Mac the startup preloader had overloaded (three models, critical pressure, swap, empty streams; docs/issues.md); both Macs were then restarted clean (a herd-node-spawned ollama serve had owned port 11434 on both since about 03:44). Both Macs then held qwen2.5:7b + qwen2.5:14b; each llama-server's prompt cache filled to its 8 GiB default, swap grew past 14 GB on s2 and each Mac went in and out of critical pressure

router_overhead.what: scripts/router_overhead.py from r1 with only s1 online: 200 alternating pairs, qwen2.5:14b, 8-token replies, direct to s1's Ollama vs through the router on r1 (router off-node, as in run 2); measured with qwen2.5:14b before the switch to qwen2.5:7b (the overhead is the router's, not the model's)
